statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or te reo Māori with Roman characters; all non-English names must adopt an approved transliteration or phonetic equivalent; names must comply with section 21 of the Companies Act 1993, avoid similarity to existing registered names, and include a required legal suffix such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', or an approved alternative.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days under section 28 of the Companies Act 1993; alternatively, a fresh name reservation application may be filed immediately; if the company name is refused due to prohibited or sensitive tokens, the applicant may request conditional approval from the relevant sector regulator (e.g., Ministry of Health for pharmaceutical logistics) and then reapply with evidence of approval; judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand may be pursued for persistent administrative refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for general corporate registration, but for GDP pharma freight logistics, physical operational premises are effectively mandatory to obtain licensing from Medsafe and to meet GDP (Good Distribution Practice) standards; a registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand, not a PO Box; virtual office may serve as registered office but a licensed operational facility is required for actual GDP activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75 percent likelihood of unannounced physical inspection; Medsafe and the New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority conduct periodic audits; the Registrar of Companies may also verify registered office and director information; GDP compliance inspections are routine for licensed distributors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) — Part 2, ss 12–25 (Incorporation), s 18 (Application for Incorporation), s 19 (Certificate of Incorporation), s 21 (Commencement of Incorporation), ss 22–24 (Company Name Restrictions and Reservation), ss 92–95 (Registered Office and Address for Service), ss 121–124 (Appointment, Powers, and Duties of Directors), s 128 (Allotment of Shares), s 151 (Requirement for a Director Resident in New Zealand), ss 156–158 (Meetings and Resolutions of the Board), Schedule 3 (Default Constitution); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (exemptions for a single founding subscriber, not applicable to regulated offers); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (customer due diligence on the corporate subscriber).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), Level 6, 15 Stout Street, Wellington 6011, New Zealand. Regulatory filings are lodged exclusively through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (New Zealand Companies Office Form NCF-1, ‘Register a Company’ electronic instrument), filed with the Companies Register and accompanied by: (i) a registered office notice (s 93), (ii) director consent forms (Director Consent to Act), (iii) shareholder consent forms, and (iv) an election to adopt the statutory default constitution in Schedule 3 of the Companies Act 1993 or an uploaded proprietary constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 1993; the company may be incorporated with zero issued share capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Companies Office for a New Zealand International Company. Consideration for issued shares may be satisfied in cash, by shareholder loan offset, or by services in kind; the terms of issue and the value of consideration must be recorded in a board resolution and contemporaneous financial records to satisfy the solvency test in s 4 of the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CK IC INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED (the ‘Company’), adopted by unanimous written resolution of the sole founding director pursuant to ss 128, 153, and 158 of the Companies Act 1993 on [Date]: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — RESOLVED that the subscriber, [Name and Address], be and is hereby allotted [Number] ordinary shares of no par value at an issue price of NZD [Amount], fully paid in consideration of [cash / shareholder loan / services-in-kind], and that the Directors make the corresponding entry in the Company’s share register (s 98); (2) REGISTERED OFFICE — RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Full Physical New Zealand Address, including street and city, not a post office box], and that the Company’s address for service and class address for service be as stated in the Application for Incorporation, or such other address as the Directors may from time to time notify to the Companies Office in accordance with ss 92–94 of the Companies Act 1993; (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS — RESOLVED that [Name], a natural person resident in New Zealand, be and is hereby appointed as Director of the Company for the purposes of s 151 of the Act; that [Name] be appointed as Chief Executive Officer; that [Name] be appointed as Company Secretary (non-statutory) and Corporate Governance Officer; and that [Name] be appointed as Responsible Person / Head of GDP Quality, who shall act as the named Qualified Person for the Company’s Licence to Deal in Medicines (Wholesale Distribution) under the Medicines Act 1981; (4) BANKING AND AUTHORISATIONS — RESOLVED that the Directors be and are hereby authorised to open one or more corporate bank accounts in the name of the Company, to sign corporate mandates, to apply for the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), to register the Company for taxation with Inland Revenue (IRD number and GST registration), and to execute all incorporation instruments, lease agreements, and licence applications necessary to carry on the business of Certified Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Clinical Logistics and Pharma Freight; (5) REVIEW OF INCORPORATION DOCUMENTS — RESOLVED that the Directors review and ratify the Application for Incorporation and the Constitution filed with the New Zealand Companies Office and that the Company records this resolution in the minutes of this first board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online ‘Name Approval’ service of the New Zealand Companies Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search against the Companies Register, the New Zealand Intellectual Property Office (NZIP) trademark database, and the Ministry of Health’s restricted-name list (names including ‘bank’, ‘insurance’, ‘trust’, or ‘pharmacy’ require prior agency consent). File an electronic name reservation application for the proposed corporate name (e.g., ‘CK IC International Company Limited’). The application must certify under s 22 of the Companies Act 1993 that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name, is not offensive, and does not contravene any enactment. If the proposed name embeds a personal name of a non-director individual, attach that individual’s written consent. Pay the name reservation fee (NZD 25.70, approximately USD 16) by credit card or POLi internet banking at the time of filing. A name so reserved is held for 20 business days.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative name (optative)
Certificate of good standing of the ultimate corporate shareholder (if name endorsement required)
Written consent of any individual whose name is used in the proposed company name
Incorporator identification (passport of the applicant or certified company extract of the body corporate applicant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is refused or queried by the Companies Office under ss 22–24 of the Act, the Registrar issues a query notice identifying the conflict. The applicant may file a written submission demonstrating the differentiating terms, a consent letter from the prior holder, or a revised ‘another name’ application within 5 working days of the query. Rejection may be reviewed by a written appeal to the Registrar; no additional fee is charged for resubmission if the same name reservation fee has been paid and the application is amended within the 20-business-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of the Incorporation Pack and Execution of Director and Shareholder Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators’ legal counsel, acting as registration agents, with the New Zealand Companies Office as the filing authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the full statutory filing pack: (i) the Companies Office Incorporation Application (Form NCF-1); (ii) a Consent to Act as Director (Form 5) executed by each proposed director, including the New Zealand-resident director required by s 151 of the Companies Act 1993; (iii) a Consent to Act as Shareholder of the founding subscriber; (iv) the Adoption of Constitution instrument — either an express election of the default constitution in Schedule 3 of the Companies Act 1993 or a fully drafted bespoke constitution, including share class rights, quorum, and officer delegation provisions compliant with the Act; (v) the Notice of registered office and address for service under s 93. Each director and shareholder must execute the consent forms before a Justice of the Peace, notary public, solicitors’ firm, or a chartered accountant member of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ). Include certified true copies of passports and proof of residential address for all directors and for any entity shareholder (board resolution and register of directors of that entity).
required_dossiers: Incorporation Application (Form NCF-1) fully completed
Consent to Act as Director (Form 5) for each director, witnessed and dated
Consent to Act as Shareholder
Constitution (custom form) or written election of the Schedule 3 default constitution
Notice of registered office (s 93 Companies Act 1993)
Certified copies of directors’ passports and recent utility bills (proof of address)
For the corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, register of directors, and resolution authorizing subscription
Completed AML/CFT ‘know your customer’ file on the founding subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Companies Office may query the application if any consent is unsigned, incorrectly witnessed, or if the registered office address is a post office box. Remedial cure: resubmit the re-executed consent forms within 10 working days of the query notice. If the query exceeds the validity date of the name reservation, a fresh name reservation (new fee) is required; the prior incorporation fee is not forfeited if the same application is corrected but may be re-applied only within the same web session repository.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of the Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — electronic incorporation lodgment portal of the Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register online portal as a filing agent or a company officer. Select ‘Register a Company’ and enter: the reserved company name; the company constitution (default or uploaded); the registered office physical address (a real, full street address in New Zealand, not a post office box); the address for service (may be the registered office or a solicitor’s address); the full legal name, date of birth, residential address, and IRD number of each director; the full share structure, including the number and class of shares allotted to the founding subscriber, total consideration, and the intended payment date; and the principal business classification (assign the ANZSIC code corresponding to ISIC 5229: ‘Freight Forwarding and Arrangement Services’ and NAICS 488510: ‘Freight Transportation Arrangement’). Upload the certified consent forms and constitution, confirm the statutory statement of compliance, and submit the application. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of NZD 105.90 (approximately USD 65.00) via POLi, credit card, or direct debit; an additional NZD 25.70 name-reservation fee is payable if not already paid. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation electronically upon satisfaction of the Act’s requirements.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation code
Completed electronic Incorporation Application fields
Constitution file (PDF) or default constitution election
Notices of director and shareholder particulars
Registered office and address for service details
Evidence of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic application is rejected for incomplete or inconsistent data (e.g., director date of birth mismatch or missing share class), the portal returns a ‘Request for More Information’ with a unique submission reference. The filing agent corrects the pinpointed fields within the same submission and resubmits without re-payment. If the rejection arises from a director residency deficiency under s 151, appoint an additional New Zealand-resident director and file an amended consent before resubmission. The 5-day SLA recommences on the date of formal resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Allocation of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (the Registrar) and the New Zealand Business Register (integrated with the Companies Register, administered by MBIE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On approval, the Registrar issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation under s 19 of the Companies Act 1993, conferring separate legal personality, perpetual succession, and limited liability on the Company from the commencement date stated in the certificate (s 21). The certificate automatically references a unique New Zealand Company Number (e.g., Company Number 9999999) and an associated New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) for use in all government and trade transactions. The incorporator must download and archive the PDF certificate, the company extract, and the filed constitution; these instruments serve as the fundamental corporate records for bank account opening, Medsafe licence applications, and freight-forwarding partner onboarding. Verify the correctness of the registered office address and the address for service as shown on the certificate; any error must be corrected by filing a notification of change under s 94 within 10 working days of discovery. The statutory registers (share register under s 98, director register under s 99, and the interests register under s 140) must be established at the registered office or an approved alternative location, and a copy of the Constitution placed in the company’s records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (electronic PDF issued by the Companies Office)
NZBN confirmation (generated automatically at incorporation)
Company extract from the Companies Register
Filed Constitution and incorporation application record
Confirmation of registered office address (lease or license to occupy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is not generated due to payment failure or a portal error, the draft application remains on the Companies Register for 7 days; re-initiate the payment step within that window. For substantive errors on the issued certificate (e.g., mis-spelling of the company name or incorrect registered office), file a ‘Rectification of Register’ notice with the Registrar under s 30 of the Companies Act 1993, supported by an application and the statutory amendment fee (NZD 17.00, approximately USD 10.00), and the Registrar will issue an amended certificate within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration (IRD Number, GST, and Employer Obligations) and Opening of the Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD) of New Zealand (PO Box 39050, Wellington Mail Centre, Lower Hutt 5045, New Zealand) and the Company’s chosen New Zealand registered bank acting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 as a reporting entity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN as a single sign-on identifier, complete the Inland Revenue business registration through the IRD’s ‘myIR’ secure portal or the Business Registration joint electronic form. Obtain the company’s IRD number (normally issued within 5 working days) and apply for GST registration if (i) taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 within any 12-month period, or (ii) the company elects voluntary GST registration under ss 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to claim input credits on the contemplated warehouse fit-out and GDP cold-chain equipment. If the company will employ staff, register for PAYE and KiwiSaver obligations. For banking, open a corporate transactional account (target rails: Swift Wire and Direct ACH) at a bank such as ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac. Present the Board Resolution of the Directors (the First Board Resolution), the Certificate of Incorporation, the NZBN number, certified passports of directors (or a notarised identification pack from the corporate shareholder), and a declaration of business purpose identifying the certified clinical logistics and GDP pharma freight activity (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510). Complete the bank’s AML/CFT customer due diligence form; the risk tier is ‘Low Risk – Standard’ as designated in the entity structure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
First Board Resolution (account signatories and banking mandate)
Certified passport copies of each director, service manager, and beneficial owner
Proof of residential address for each beneficial owner
Certificate of good standing of the non-resident corporate shareholder (if any)
Statement of intended business purpose (GDP Pharma Freight logistics)
Lease or agreement showing the warehouse business premises in New Zealand
GST and IRD registration confirmations as issued by Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a compliance query (e.g., unresolved IRD number for a foreign director or missing certification), produce the notarised foreign passport translation and resubmit through the myIR message centre; the IRD number is released within 5 working days of rectification. If the bank declines the account application due to the non-resident ownership structure or perceived economic substance concerns, strengthen the submission by providing: (i) the executed lease for the New Zealand logistics warehouse; (ii) the provisional Medsafe licence application receipt; (iii) a letter from the New Zealand resident director confirming management control; and (iv) the Company’s forecast cash-flow and GDP service agreements. If the decline persists, approach the bank’s appeals committee or open a secondary account at a challenger bank licensed in New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Maintenance of Corporate Registers, Constitution Custody, and Corporate Governance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and Company Secretary of the Company, reporting to the New Zealand Companies Office for any post-incorporation changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Constitute the physical or electronic statutory registers in accordance with the Companies Act 1993: the share register (s 98), the director register (s 99), the interests register (s 140), the minute book of board and shareholder resolutions, and (if adopted) the board’s authorisation register. Record the issue of share certificates to the founding subscriber. Lodge a notice of any change in directors, registered office, or address for service with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the change using Company Office Form 10 (Change of Director) or the online change service. Adopt the internal management policies applicable to a GDP pharma freight operator: the sealed Constitution, the corporate seal (if any), the board delegation policy, the AML/CFT programme, the whistle-blower policy, and the conflict-of-interest register. Schedule an annual board cycle with an ethics committee meeting (no dividend policy until solvency tests are met). The governance officer must file an annual return with the Companies Office before the anniversary of incorporation (fee NZD 45.00 per year) and ensure the company maintains a New Zealand registered office open for service of process.
required_dossiers: Constitution (final executed copy, sealed and lodged)
Share certificates countersigned by the directors
Statutory registers: share register, director register, interests register, and minutes
First Board Resolution in the minute book
AML/CFT customer due diligence file on the founding subscriber and beneficial owners
Evidence of the registered office (lease or license to occupy)
Annual return calendar entry and Companies Office filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a compliance reminder for failure to file an annual return or maintaining a valid registered office, file the overdue annual return online immediately and pay the late fee (NZD 45.00 standard plus any arrears). If a director becomes non-resident and the company ceases to satisfy s 151 of the Act, the Registrar may issue a notice of breach; the company must appoint a new New Zealand-resident director within 15 working days and file the updated consent forms. If an interest-register omission is identified, the directors must record the late entry with an explanatory minute and, where material, rectify the register under s 30 with notice to the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medsafe — New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority, Ministry of Health, Level 6, 133 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand; operational enforcement is delegated to the Medicines Control section of Medsafe and the district health boards’ medicines compliance inspectors.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence to Deal in Medicines (Wholesale Distribution / Dealer’s Licence) granted under ss 32 and 39 of the Medicines Act 1981, together with a Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Compliance Certificate in accordance with the Medsafe ‘Guide to Good Distribution Practice for Medicines’ (based on the PIC/S GDP Guidelines and the WHO Technical Report Series No. 957, Annex 5). The licence is supplementary to the Customs and Excise Act 2018 bonded freight status if the Company acts as a customs-approved depot for controlled medicines.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand for hazardous-substances matters under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act 1996, together with the relevant regional council and territorial authority (city or district council) acting under the Resource Management Act 1991, the Building Act 2004, and the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — Permitted Activity (Low Environmental Impact) for a GDP freight forwarding and clinical logistics warehouse. The proposed activity constitutes a ‘Permitted Activity’ under the operative District Plan (Logistics / Warehouse Use zone); no resource consent is required for the storage and onward freight of pharmaceutical products at ambient temperature-controlled conditions. A Separate ‘HSNO Compliance Certificate’ is generally not required where quantities of hazardous substances (e.g., cytotoxic medicines, refrigerants from pharmaceutical cold-chain units, or anaesthetic gases) remain below the HSNO trigger thresholds in Schedule 1 of the Hazardous Substances (Classes 1–5) Regulations 2001. If the Company elects to store schedule 8 controlled drugs or significant quantities of flammable refrigerants (R290 or R600A recovered from cold-chain units), a full ‘HSNO Substance Approval and Location Compliance Certificate’ is required. A full Environmental Impact Assessment (AEE) under the RMA is triggered only when constructing a new warehouse exceeding the permitted building bulk, when undertaking works in a flood plain or a sensitive airshed, or when a wastewater discharge to land or water is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic sanitary wastewater may discharge to the municipal sewer without a trade waste consent; any pharmaceutical wash-down water or decontamination effluent must be sampled and must satisfy the local trade waste limits, typically (i) pH between 6.0 and 9.5, (ii) chemical oxygen demand (COD) below 300 mg/L, (iii) total suspended solids below 350 mg/L, (iv) fats, oils, and grease below 50 mg/L, and (v) no free cyanide or halogenated organic compounds above detection limits; the Company must obtain a ‘Trade Waste Discharge Consent’ from the territorial authority before any high-strength effluent enters the sewer. Air and VOCs: the cold-chain hydrocarbon refrigerants (flashpoint below 61°C) are class 3.1A substances and must be stored in approved HSNO-compliant cylinders with ventilation meeting the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004; VOC content limits of 200 g/m³ apply to any sterilant or cleaning agents used on site; diesel-powered forklift emissions must meet the NES-AQ particulate thresholds and the forklifts must be serviced on an annual schedule. Solid waste: all cytotoxic or hazardous pharmaceutical waste must be segregated, labelled as HSNO class 6.1/6.9, and removed by an approved licensed waste transporter under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances (Disposal) Regulations 2004, with a consignment note retained for 7 years and disposed of at an EPA-approved facility; temperature-controlled waste (expired vaccines and biologics) must be denatured before disposal and recorded in the waste register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: the warehouse and office premises must obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness (Form 12) issued by the building owner under the Building Act 2004 and the Building (New Zealand Building Code) Regulations 1992; the warrant must include the annual Fire Safety Certificate issued by a qualified IQP (Independent Qualified Person) confirming the sprinkler system, fire hydrants, and fire alarm monitoring are compliant with the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Act 2017; a Fire Evacuation Scheme must be approved by FENZ where more than 10 persons are present. An annual ‘Form 11A’ building inspection record must be kept. Structural and Load Clearance: a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) must certify the warehouse floor loads and pallet racking seismic restraint in accordance with AS/NZS 1170.0-2002 and NZS 1170.5-2004; the racking installation must be undertaken by a certified racking engineering contractor and a certificate of seismic compliance for a 5000-pallet high-bay configuration must be on file. Occupational and Workplace Clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand registration under the Health and Safety at Work at Work Act 2015 is automatic on commencement of business, but the Company must prepare a Site Specific Safety Plan (SSSP) that includes: (i) a controlled-temperature pharmaceutical storage zone validated at 15–25°C (or 2–8°C for refrigerated clinical logistics) with continuous data logging and an alarm response plan; (ii) a quarantine area for temperature excursion stock; (iii) forklift operator certificates with a valid F-endorsed licence issued by a WorkSafe-accredited tertiary provider; (iv) manual handling and fit-to-work medical clearances for warehouse operatives; (v) spill containment and PPE protocols for pharmaceutical spillage; and (vi) a health and safety induction log and emergency response team certification. A separate ‘worker engagement and participation’ system must be documented, and hazardous substances must be segregated in a dedicated HSNO-approved caged area with a secondary containment racetrack.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke / Inland Revenue) - official government portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz; corporate registry: New Zealand Companies Office at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; customs electronic platform: NZ Customs Trade Single Window
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Stage 1: File the overseas company incorporation or foreign company registration with the New Zealand Companies Office to obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); Stage 2: Apply for the statutory IRD number (TIN) through myIR using the non-resident company registration stream, submitting certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitution, director register and ultimate beneficial owner identification; IRD automatically matches the NZBN and issues an 8-9 digit IRD number; Stage 3: Register separately for GST online in myIR (GST registration section) - no separate VAT registration number is issued; the GST account is linked to the same IRD number and serves as the New Zealand GST ID for cross-border invoicing and customs purposes. If the CK_IC is structured as a Cook Islands International Company operating under the Tax_Exempt_Zone profile, it is not required to register with the Inland Revenue for income tax unless it derives New Zealand-source income; however, NZ GST registration is mandatory once the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand and meets the NZD 60,000 registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections under New Zealand law: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 for a closely-held New Zealand-resident International Company, rendering it fiscally transparent; (2) GST group registration election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to consolidate related NZ entities; (3) consolidated group election for wholly-owned corporate groups under subpart FG of the Income Tax Act 2007; (4) hybrid mismatch ordering elections under the BEPS hybrid rules (Part FH of the Income Tax Act 2007); and (5) for the Tax_Exempt_Zone IC profile, a non-resident company may rely on the territorial attribution rules so that foreign-source income is excluded from New Zealand corporate tax, provided it elects or confirms that it has no fixed establishment in New Zealand and conducts no New Zealand-source taxable supplies beyond permitted thresholds. New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.ird_number_format_note: New Zealand IRD numbers are 8 or 9 digits; foreign non-resident companies may be issued an IRD number with the standard format, and the number is used for both income tax and GST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.gst_registration_threshold_confirmation: The mandatory GST registration threshold is NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available to non-resident businesses carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand. Non-resident suppliers of remote or digital services must register on a NZD 60,000 global-supplies basis when supplying B2C remote services to New Zealand consumers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (mandatory registration); voluntary registration is available to non-resident businesses carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand; non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services must register on a NZD 60,000 global-supplies basis when supplying B2C remote services to New Zealand consumers
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate exists under New Zealand law. GST invoices must satisfy section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and be issued within 28 days of the supply. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network under the New Zealand Peppol Authority. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR on a two-month or six-month filing cycle; Inland Revenue performs data matching and risk-based audit selection, but there is no API-based pre-clearance stamping, digital watermark, or invoice-by-invoice fiscal approval mechanism applicable to B2B exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% GST) applies to: (a) goods physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier, where the goods are exported within the required timeframe and the supplier retains evidence of export (GST Act 1985 section 11(1)(a)); (b) services supplied to a non-resident where the services are not physically performed in New Zealand and are directly in connection with goods situated outside New Zealand at the time of supply (section 11A); (c) international freight, transport and insurance services in respect of exported goods, including GDP pharma logistics, where the freight forwarder demonstrates that title, control and risk in the pharmaceutical cargo pass to the overseas consignee and that the cargo physically departs New Zealand; and (d) supplies to non-residents that are expressly zero-rated by Gazette exemption under the GST Act. Eligibility for the CK_IC requires the entity to hold a valid zero-rating certificate, verify the non-resident status of the recipient, and maintain a complete audit trail of export logistics, including time-stamped departure evidence; pure domestic storage or handling of pharma goods inside New Zealand for a New Zealand principal is taxable at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (NZ Customs electronic export entry filed through the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign currency bank confirmation evidencing offshore payment
Commercial invoice and signed GST zero-rating certificate (section 11(1) statement)
Non-resident recipient/supplier declaration confirming offshore status and taxable activity
GDP temperature-monitored transport/reconciliation log and pharma cargo integrity certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess incorrectly zero-rated supplies within four years of the assessment date, extended to seven years for gross carelessness or evasion, and with no time limit where no return has been filed; clawback of GST at 15% plus use-of-money interest applies. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 escalate from 20% (lack of reasonable care or unacceptable tax position) to 100% (abusive tax position) and 150% (evasion). Fraudulent export zero-rating documentation exposes the CK_IC to criminal liability under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, including fines up to NZD 50,000 per conviction for the company and imprisonment for responsible individuals, together with NZ Customs enforcement under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, including seizure of cargo, suspension of export privileges, and imposition of penalties for false export declarations as to destination, value, or pharmaceutical cargo status. Although New Zealand law does not prescribe a 180-day inward remittance statute, banking and transfer pricing practice treats remittance within 180 days as the documentary benchmark; failure to repatriate consideration within that window may trigger substantive review and reversal of the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a free-floating currency regime with full current and capital account convertibility. There is no exchange-control legislation restricting the inflow or outflow of foreign currency, and the New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely tradable on global markets. Profit remittances and capital repatriations are subject to no quantitative restrictions; the only statutory filters are the Overseas Investment Act 2005 (which screens foreign acquisitions of sensitive land and significant business assets, generally NZD 200 million or above for treaty partners) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (which governs customer due diligence at the banking intermediary level). A non-resident Cook Islands International Company (Tax_Exempt_Zone classification) faces no convertibility hurdle for dividend, interest, or equity capital flows, and the New Zealand income tax system does not impose a branch-remittance barrier on non-resident treasury accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement under New Zealand law to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline for bringing export receipts onshore. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings in offshore bank accounts indefinitely, provided those earnings are properly declared for income tax and covered under the Controlled Foreign Company and transfer-pricing rules where applicable. For this GDP pharma freight structure, freight forwarding fees and logistics reimbursements from non-resident clients may be credited directly to the IC's offshore or onshore NZD foreign-currency account without Reserve Bank reporting, although NZ banks will apply domestic International Transactions Reporting (ITR) thresholds (typically NZD 10,000 per transaction) for balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulatory_notes: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 provides the prudential framework, but it imposes no transactional FX approval or licensing requirement on ordinary trade settlements. Derivatives and hedging activities by non-bank corporates are unregulated unless the entity becomes a licensed 'non-bank deposit taker' or a Financial Markets Authority (FMA) regulated derivatives issuer; a plain treasury hedging programme with bank counterparties falls outside licensing scope.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.profit_remittance_hurdles: No exchange-control approval is required for profit or dividend remittances. The sole monetary friction is non-resident withholding tax (NRWT): NZ-source dividends, interest, and royalties paid to a non-resident are subject to NRWT at 30%, 15%, and 15% respectively, unless reduced under an applicable double-tax agreement. A Cook Islands International Company with Tax_Exempt_Zone status and no New Zealand-source income is outside the NRWT net entirely; payments made from its NZD operational account to third-party freight providers are treasury disbursements, not assessable remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in NZD and USD (Global Plus platform)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.institutional_notes: Strong trade finance franchise and dedicated non-resident IC onboarding unit in Auckland. Supports SWIFT MT103, MT700, and multi-currency sweep; accepts electronic onboarding with professional introducer for Cook Islands ICs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (Commonwealth Bank of Australia subsidiary)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and NZD Foreign Currency Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.institutional_notes: Streamlined corporate onboarding with documented confidence of CDD for Cook Islands ICs under a chain of ownership declaration to UBOs. Good FX pricing for NZD/USD and inward investment purpose code filing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for security deposits / customs bonds
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.institutional_notes: BNZ's institutional and trade logistics desk handles goods distribution undertakings; escrow and deferred-payment instruments are commonplace for pharmaceutical GDP freight. Remote onboarding allowed with New Zealand-registered legal counsel certification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with dedicated SWIFT BIC (WPACNZ2W)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.institutional_notes: Strong Australasian payment rails and direct participation in NZ's BECS (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) for domestic ACH; supports ISO20022 and treasury APIs. High tolerance for export-led logistics treasury flows.

Kiwibank has a conservative risk appetite for non-resident tax-exempt structures; may require a New Zealand director or a physical New Zealand business address. Suitable as a secondary local clearing account rather than primary treasury vehicle.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border financial technology EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) such as Airwallex (registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register), Wise NZ, and OFX provide viable ancillary clearing capacity for low-value freight disbursements and supplier payments. Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for operational transactions, LOW for escrow or capital injection vehicles. Legal constraint: no EMI may hold a New Zealand banking licence; they are non-deposit-taking financial service providers supervised by the FMA under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and are required to meet AML-CFT obligations. Because the underlying business is GDP pharma freight (Low_Risk_Standard AML tier), an EMI may be used for routine disbursement rails, but the primary settlement ledger must be held with a licensed New Zealand registered bank to ensure MT103 settlement finality and to satisfy customs and pharmacovigilance audit trails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand statutory law does not mandate a physical in-person interview for corporate bank account opening. However, in practice, the AML-CFT regime and bank internal policies require for a non-resident International Company structure: (i) a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and good standing, (ii) the corporate register extract identifying directors and shareholders, and (iii) a registered professional introducer (New Zealand law firm or Big-4 accounting firm) to certify the identity of signatories. Most tier-1 banks allow fully remote onboarding with video-conference verification and electronic signatures (NZ Electronic Transactions Act 2002), but they will require a physical or digital meeting with the ultimate beneficial owners if the IC is held through a trust or nominee layer. A Cook Islands IC with Tax_Exempt_Zone classification can be opened 100% remotely if the professional introducer provides a legal opinion confirming substance status; otherwise, a single physical visit by the compliance officer or an in-country local director is pragmatically required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company (Cook Islands) with no New Zealand economic substance, nominated as the freight intermediary for pharmaceutical goods
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing from the Cook Islands Registrar of International Companies; (2) a New Zealand tax opinion confirming the IC's non-resident tax-exempt status and absence of a permanent establishment; (3) the registered office service agreement with a licensed Cook Islands trust company; (4) a letter of economic substance declaring the board meeting location, custody of records, and treasury decision-making; (5) the GDP (Good Distribution Practice) certificate issued by a recognised regulatory authority for the pharma freight scope; (6) a local New Zealand logistics agency agreement giving the IC a factual nexus to the staged ISIC_5229 freight arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership obscured through a discretionary trust or corporate nominee shareholders (common in CK_IC structures)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) A full trust deed and a sealed declaration of trust naming the settlor, protector, and discretionary beneficiaries (or a redacted extract if confidentiality statute applies, supplemented by a lawyer's opinion); (2) a 100% chain-of-title analysis from the IC down to the underlying natural persons, presented on a bank-approved UBO spreadsheet; (3) passport copies and address verification for every natural-person UBO with ≥10% interest or control; (4) a negative-media and sanctions screening report from a credible provider (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones); (5) a signed source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements of the originator; (6) where the UBO is a New Zealand ADB (Asia-Pacific agriculture/food) investor, a reference letter from an existing banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Freight-forwarding payment pattern characterised by 'pass-through' book transfers (funds received from pharma principals and immediately disbursed to airlines, customs brokers, and cold-chain depots), which may indicate offshore cash-funnel risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed GDP pharma logistics contracts with the cargo owner or its authorised broker; (2) airway bills, customs declarations, and temperature-record charts from continuous data loggers to evidence genuine transshipment; (3) a treasury policy document prohibiting third-party routing (i.e., all settlement counterparties must be named in the transaction chain); (4) a pro-forma invoice and client billing schedule showing the commission or fee mark-up structure; (5) a minimum documentary guideline requiring a supplier invoice, proof of shipment, and pre-approval for any disbursement exceeding NZD 50,000; (6) a historical bank statement from the IC's operating jurisdiction demonstrating a consistent trade-flow pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: New Zealand banks' internal 'Enhanced Due Diligence – Offshore Financial Centre' flag triggered by the Cook Islands jurisdiction code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) a legal opinion from a New Zealand-licensed barrister establishing that the Cook Islands IC is not presumed criminal and holds no automatic high-risk classification under the AML-CFT Regulations 2011; (2) evidence that the IC is not a 'shell bank' and maintains substantial physical office presence in the Cook Islands or a satisfactory dedicated trustee arrangement; (3) independent audit reports (IFRS or equivalent) for the last two years; (4) certificates of tax compliance from the Cook Islands Ministry of Finance; (5) a written attestation that the IC does not issue bearer shares and has migrated to a fully dematerialised shareholder register; (6) an introduction letter from the bank's own Auckland branch through the client-offshore-onshore referral channel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial capital injection from the parent or beneficial owner to the NZ operating treasury account must be executed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 with full remitter detail. New Zealand banks require a purpose-of-payment code under the International Transactions Reporting (ITR) framework: use code 'FDI – Equity Capital' (inward direct investment into a resident enterprise) if the IC is registered as an NZ branch; if the capital is held offshore and used to fund a New Zealand trust, use code 'Trust Increase in Liability' or the specific FMA-approved narrative. The compliant protocol is: (i) the remittance must originate from a bank account in the name of the declarant shareholder, never from a third-party aggregator; (ii) the reference field must cite the IC's unique identifier and the words 'Capital Escrow – GDP Freight Validation', (iii) supporting board resolution, subscription agreement, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's no-objection implicit posture are transmitted to the receiving bank in advance; (iv) amounts above NZD 100,000 per single credit may require the bank to file a Reportable Transaction summary and source-of-funds confirmation, though no prior exchange-control approval is required; (v) for currency conversion, the NZD/USD spot trade must be booked through the receiving bank to create a single audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for GDP pharma freight—covering airfreight, cold-chain storage, customs duties, and inland cartage—are cleared through four rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for international supplier payments (airline cargo carriers, overseas pharma forwarders), with a strict 24-hour execution window and a standing instruction to append the pharma product NDC or freight-airway number in payment narrative; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) for high-value imports of temperature-controlled packaging materials where the logistics provider is not yet a trusted counterparty; (3) NZ BECS (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) for domestic NZD vendor payments, executed as Direct ACH (Direct Credit) with the four-digit PHARM-GDP reconciliation reference; and (4) same-day High-Value Clearing System (HVCS) for urgent settlements above NZD 500,000 to customs brokers or cargo terminal operators. All outbound payments must be matched against an approved purchase order and a goods-receipt confirmation generated by the GDP manual; the treasury policy disallows unearmarked 'general sweep' transfers, and every MT103 must carry a BIC-validated beneficiary account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC Forward (Plain Vanilla NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR) – permitted for balancing the receivable-denominated treaty of sale when the pharma freight client is invoiced in USD while the airlines bill in NZD; must be transacted on ISDA or NZ-documentation master agreement and fully covered by underlying exposure
Window Forward Contracts – permitted to hedge a portfolio of uncertain inbound remittances arising from third-party logistics quarterly reconciliations
FX Swap (Swap Against Spot) – permitted for temporary bridging of NZD liquidity into USD for weekend warehouse duty payments, closed within one month
Cross-Currency Swap – permitted for a single-medium-term USD liability of the IC's foreign-currency bank loan, if any, with interest and principal exchanged via two residual spot conversions

Vanilla Exchange-Traded and OTC Options (Zebra and Call/Put structures) – permissible only for hedging recognised freight tender bids, and subject to FMA derivative issuance rules if the IC becomes a regular issuer; an IC using options purely for hedging trade lines under ISDA 2002 with a NZ registered bank is exempt from FMA licensing

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) generally NOT required for NZD because the NZD is freely deliverable; prohibited as speculative positional hedging under the corporate treasury mandate unless expressly approved by the board and booked with a bank licensed in New Zealand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 216) including confirmation of registered office, directors, shareholders, and constitution details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment - MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within 10 working days after the company's annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation as stated in the Companies Office return notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts late-filing penalties and director fines up to NZD 10,000; the Registrar may issue a 20-working-day notice of intention to remove the company from the Companies Register, leading to administrative strike-off and asset forfeiture to the Crown

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and, where applicable, auditor's report (Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) and Inland Revenue (IRD) where filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved and filed within 5 months of the balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, the filing/IRD requirement aligns with the tax return date of 7 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing is a continuing offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; directors may be fined up to NZD 30,000 plus NZD 500 per day while the default continues, and the company may be procedurally struck off for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return and terminal/provisional tax payment obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, the annual tax return is due by 7 July; terminal tax is due by 7 April in the following income year; provisional tax instalments are due per the IRD schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a late-filing penalty, late payment penalties of 4% immediately due plus 1% per month, and Use-of-Money Interest (UOMI) on unpaid tax; IRD may institute direct recovery action against the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medicines Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Licence / Wholesale Distribution Certification — annual renewal or validation confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority (Medsafe), Ministry of Health
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal/validation must be completed before the licence anniversary; applications for renewal are generally due no later than 30 days before expiry for continued GDP certification in the pharma freight scope
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating, storing, or transporting medicines for distribution without a current applicable licence/certification is an offence under the Medicines Act 1981; penalties include fines up to NZD 250,000, suspension/revocation of the GDP certificate, and cessation of lawful pharma logistics operations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is compulsory for a New Zealand company that is not a 'small company' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 — i.e., where for both current and preceding balance dates the company exceeds at least one of: total assets exceeding NZD 60 million; total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million; or 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees. Audit is also mandatory for FMC reporting entities and for any company in respect of which shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights have validly requested audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); for-profit entities apply New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS 1-20), with reduced disclosure and differential reporting concessions available for Tier 2 non-publicly-accountable entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a public standalone UBO return; however, the annual return to the Companies Office requires confirmation of current shareholders, directors, and registered office, and every share transfer must be entered in the members register and notified to the Companies Office in a timely manner. Where the entity is an AML/CFT reporting business, beneficial ownership must be verified under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and reviewed at least annually and on any material ownership change; the Companies Office record of ultimate shareholding must be kept true and accurate
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholders' and directors' meetings and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,200 per annum for a New Zealand registered office and company secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per annum for a certified GDP clinical logistics company, depending on transaction volume, controlled-temperature inventory, and group reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A, clause 2; standard company tax rate for the 2023-24 through 2025-26 income years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand's core reliefs: (a) full imputation system - company tax attaches as imputation credits to resident shareholders, eliminating double taxation; (b) R&D Tax Incentive - 15% refundable tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure; (c) no general capital gains tax, with limited exceptions (financial arrangements, revenue account property); (d) non-resident International Company (IC) incorporated offshore and managed/controlled outside New Zealand is taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income; (e) transitional resident exemption for new migrants holding foreign interests; (f) Approved Issuer Levy of 2% payable in lieu of NRWT on eligible cross-border interest; (g) tax losses carry forward indefinitely with no 5-year statutory expiry, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test and, for loss companies with greater than 49% continuity breach, the business continuity test (s IA 5, Income Tax Act 2007).
